Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

concern noun and verb

worry

also be concerned, concerned

classical

Ter. And. 304: lassus, cūrā cōnfectus
Traupman 150, 294
Traupman 295

cūra, cūrae f.

noun, first declension

concern, worry, anxiety

Also care in the good sense, the attention one gives a thing.

Other words

  • labōrāre dē (+ ablative) — be concerned about, be anxious about

    phrase: labōrō with dē and the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: nihil labōrō, nisi ut salvus sīs; Traupman 95: labōrō nōn valdē dē …; Traupman 295

    Nihil labōrō, it doesn’t trouble me; with dē, of what one is anxious about (Lewis & Short).

  • sollicitus, sollicita, sollicitum — worried, concerned (dē + ablative)

    declension · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.6.120: nōn sollicitus; Traupman 23, 294; Traupman 295

  • sollicitō, sollicitāre, sollicitāvī, sollicitātum — worry, trouble (someone): “it concerns me”

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 162: quid tē ergō aliud sollicitat?; Traupman 294; Traupman 295

  • sollicitūdō, sollicitūdinis f. — anxiety, worry

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.18: sollicitūdō aegritūdō cum cōgitātiōne, anxiety is distress with brooding

Examples

  • nihil labōrō, nisi ut salvus sīs

    my only concern is that you should be wellCic. Fam. 16.4.4

  • deinde eō dormītum, nōn sollicitus, mihi quod crās surgendum sit māne

    then I go off to sleep, not worried that I have to get up early tomorrowHor. S. 1.6.119–120

  • Avia, quae dē illā domō nōn minus quam ipse labōrābat

    Grandma, who was no less concerned about that house than he wasLibellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

See also concern, be afraid, care.
